"The one-horned rhinoceros is found in (A) ______ National Park in Assam. Cheetahs were brought back to India in 2022 at (B) ______ National Park."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is India called a megadiverse country? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Kaziranga (ii) Kuno (iii) (1) It has a large share of the world's plant and animal species. (2) Its varied climate and relief support many ecosystems.
items.markingKey: (i) Kaziranga – 1 mark. (ii) Kuno – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) It has a large share of the world's plant and animal species. (2) Its varied climate and relief support many ecosystems.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: Teak and sal are important trees of the tropical deciduous forests.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. Teak and sal are important trees of the tropical deciduous forests.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'mangrove forests'?
items.answer: Tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans
items.markingKey: (a) 'Mangrove forests' means tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans
A large natural region with a distinct type of climate, vegetation and animal life
A region very rich in species, many found nowhere else, that is under threat
Species brought from elsewhere that spread and harm local plants and animals

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Poaching
2. Endemic species
3. Food chain
4. Ecosystem
Column B:
(p) A community of living things interacting with each other and with their non-living environment
(q) Species found only in one particular area
(r) Illegal hunting or capture of wild animals
(s) A sequence showing who eats whom, starting with a green plant
items.markingKey: (b) Poaching – illegal hunting or capture of wild animals; Endemic species – species found only in one particular area; Food chain – a sequence showing who eats whom, starting with a green plant; Ecosystem – a community of living things interacting with each other and with their non-living environment.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was passed in 1972.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. The Wildlife (Protection) Act was passed in 1972.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
I. Project Tiger
II. Wildlife (Protection) Act
III. Cheetahs reintroduced at Kuno
IV. Nilgiri, the first biosphere reserve
items.answer: II, I, IV, III
items.markingKey: (c) Wildlife (Protection) Act (1972); Project Tiger (1973); Nilgiri, the first biosphere reserve (1986); Cheetahs reintroduced at Kuno (2022).

items.stem: Fill in the blank: India has ______ of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots.
items.answer: four
items.markingKey: India has four of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots. (1 mark)

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Mangrove forests
2. Project Tiger
3. Invasive species
4. Decomposers
Column B:
(p) Species brought from elsewhere that spread and harm local plants and animals
(q) Organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals
(r) The conservation programme launched in 1973 to save tigers in reserves
(s) Tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans
items.markingKey: (c) Mangrove forests – tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans; Project Tiger – the conservation programme launched in 1973 to save tigers in reserves; Invasive species – species brought from elsewhere that spread and harm local plants and animals; Decomposers – organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'biodiversity hotspot'?
items.answer: A region very rich in species, many found nowhere else, that is under threat
items.markingKey: (c) 'Biodiversity hotspot' means a region very rich in species, many found nowhere else, that is under threat; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Tidal forests of coastal deltas, such as the Sundarbans
Organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals
A region very rich in species, many found nowhere else, that is under threat
The variety of plants, animals and micro-organisms in a region

items.stem: On an outline political map of India, locate and label the following: (a) The Western Ghats evergreen forests (b) The thorn forests of Rajasthan (c) The Sundarbans
items.answer: (a) Western Ghats – along the west coast (b) western Rajasthan – Rajasthan (c) Sundarbans – West Bengal
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct location: (a) Western Ghats – along the west coast (b) western Rajasthan – Rajasthan (c) Sundarbans – West Bengal

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 9 student on "The biosphere and ecosystems" and answer the questions that follow.
"Bacteria and fungi that break down dead matter are (A) ______. Only about (B) ______ per cent of energy is passed on from one level of a food chain to the next."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why are decomposers important in an ecosystem? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) decomposers (ii) 10 (iii) (1) They break down dead plants and animals. (2) They return nutrients to the soil for plants to use.
items.markingKey: (i) decomposers – 1 mark. (ii) 10 – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) They break down dead plants and animals. (2) They return nutrients to the soil for plants to use.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'decomposers'?
items.answer: Organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals
items.markingKey: (a) 'Decomposers' means organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals
Illegal hunting or capture of wild animals
A sequence showing who eats whom, starting with a green plant
The variety of plants, animals and micro-organisms in a region

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Tropical deciduous forests
2. Biosphere
3. Thorn forests
4. Endemic species
Column B:
(p) The narrow zone of the Earth where land, water and air meet and support life
(q) Forests of thorny trees and bushes in areas with less than 70 cm of rainfall
(r) Monsoon forests that shed leaves in the dry season, such as teak and sal forests
(s) Species found only in one particular area
items.markingKey: (b) Tropical deciduous forests – monsoon forests that shed leaves in the dry season, such as teak and sal forests; Biosphere – the narrow zone of the Earth where land, water and air meet and support life; Thorn forests – forests of thorny trees and bushes in areas with less than 70 cm of rainfall; Endemic species – species found only in one particular area.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: Cheetahs were brought back to India in 2022 at Kuno National Park.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. Cheetahs were brought back to India in 2022 at Kuno National Park.

items.stem: Identify the correct term for the following description: Forests of thorny trees and bushes in areas with less than 70 cm of rainfall.
items.answer: Thorn forests
items.markingKey: (a) Thorn forests: forests of thorny trees and bushes in areas with less than 70 cm of rainfall.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 9 student on "Threats to biodiversity and conservation efforts" and answer the questions that follow.
"Project Elephant was launched in (A) ______. The (B) ______ is a critically endangered bird found mainly in Rajasthan."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is biodiversity declining? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 1992 (ii) Great Indian Bustard (iii) (1) Forests are cleared for farms, mines and towns. (2) Poaching, pollution and invasive species.
items.markingKey: (i) 1992 – 1 mark. (ii) Great Indian Bustard – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Forests are cleared for farms, mines and towns. (2) Poaching, pollution and invasive species.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: Many interlinked food chains together form a food web.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. Many interlinked food chains together form a food web.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 9 student on "Major biomes of the world and natural vegetation of India" and answer the questions that follow.
"Tropical evergreen forests grow where rainfall is more than (A) ______ cm. Sundari trees are found in the (B) ______ forests."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why do tropical deciduous trees shed their leaves? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 200 (ii) mangrove (iii) (1) To reduce loss of water in the dry season. (2) There is not enough water for leaves throughout the year.
items.markingKey: (i) 200 – 1 mark. (ii) mangrove – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) To reduce loss of water in the dry season. (2) There is not enough water for leaves throughout the year.
